bull.b: Sustained high top-line growth indicates clear market demand for Surf Air's regional and charter offerings. Over 2–6 months this underpins scale opportunities, supports unit economics improvement if margins expand, and provides a revenue base to fund SurfOS rollout and electrification investments.

Commercial traction for SurfOS (BrokerOS) creates a higher-margin, recurring revenue stream separate from flying operations. Durable productivity gains for brokers and enterprise pipeline (Wheels Up deal) can scale SaaS-like margins and diversify cash flow over the medium term.

Restructuring convertible and term debt to longer maturities materially reduces near-term amortization and refinancing pressure. That structural improvement increases runway, lowers immediate liquidity risk, and gives time to execute SurfOS commercialization and operational cost saves.

bear.b: Negative equity and sizable leverage materially constrain financial flexibility, raise refinancing and dilution risk, and limit capacity for capital-intensive initiatives. Over months, this can force costly financing, restrict strategic options, and heighten vulnerability to adverse shocks.

Persistently large negative operating and free cash flows mean the business requires ongoing external funding to sustain growth and electrification plans. This structural cash deficit increases dilution risk, limits reinvestment capacity, and pressures liquidity if refinancing windows close.

Dependence on multi-year certification and demonstration timelines makes expected cost and emission benefits uncertain. Delays would defer capex savings and SurfOS synergies tied to electrified fleet, extending reliance on capital markets and operational transition risks for years.
